title: What Do You Think?
subtitle: カレー・シャツ・ばんごはん・えいが
review: Kana, kanji, notes, translations and questions written by Claude. The Japanese, the romaji and the humor have not been checked by a Japanese speaker. English support only: no Burmese lines yet.
intro: A curry with three apples in it, a shirt that looked better yesterday, a dinner where anything is fine except everything, and a film Emi may have slept through: four short scenes between Emi and Riku. Listen for dō? and dō omou? when they ask, for … to omou when they answer, and for chotto…, the sentence nobody finishes.

lines.note: A, dō?: how is A? The shortest way to ask for an opinion.
Un: a casual yes. Yo at the end: I'm telling you.

lines.kana: ほんとう。でも、ちょっと…
lines.note: Chotto…, left unfinished, is the polite way to say there is a problem.

lines.kana: ちょっとあまいかなとおもって。
lines.say: ちょっと甘いかなと思って。

tr.en: I just thought it might be a little sweet.

lines.note: … to omou: I think that… Kana softens it: maybe. Omotte, left open, softens it again.
Ireru: to put in. N da explains. Apple is a well-known secret ingredient of Japanese curry.
Nanko: how many. -ko counts small round things such as apples.

lines.romaji: Sore wa mō, dezāto da to omou.
lines.kana: それはもう、デザートだとおもう。
lines.say: それはもう、デザートだと思う。

tr.en: Then I think it's a dessert.

lines.note: Noun + da to omou: I think it is… Mō here: by now, already.

lines.kana: このシャツ、どうおもう？

tr.en: What do you think of this shirt?

lines.note: Dō omou?: what do you think? Word for word: how do you think?
Ii n ja nai?: isn't it good? A mild yes, often said without much feeling.
Homeru: to praise. Homete ru?: are you praising me?

lines.kana: わるくないとおもうよ。
lines.note: Warukunai: not bad. Adjective + to omou: I think it's…

lines.romaji: Demo, watashi wa kinō no shatsu no hō ga suki kana.
lines.kana: でも、わたしはきのうのシャツのほうがすきかな。
lines.say: でも、私は昨日のシャツの方が好きかな。

tr.en: But I think I like yesterday's shirt better.

lines.note: Watashi wa: as for me. A no hō ga suki: I like A better. Kana: I suppose.

tr.en: I wore this one yesterday too.

lines.note: Mo: too, also. Word for word: yesterday too, it was this one.

lines.romaji: … Ja, kinō no hō ga niatte ta.
lines.kana: …じゃ、きのうのほうがにあってた。
lines.say: …じゃ、昨日の方が似合ってた。
lines.note: Niau: to suit someone. Niatte ta: it suited you.

lines.kana: ばんごはん、なにがいい？

tr.en: What do you want for dinner?

lines.note: Nani ga ii?: what would be good? The everyday way to ask what someone would like.
Nan demo: anything. Nan demo ii: anything is fine.
A wa?: how about A?
A wa chotto…: the polite no. Nobody finishes the sentence.
Dō kana: I wonder. Another soft no.
Desho: you know that, right? Short for deshō.

lines.romaji: Nan demo ii tte itta yo ne.
lines.kana: なんでもいいっていったよね。
lines.say: 何でもいいって言ったよね。
lines.note: … tte itta: you said that… Yo ne checks that the other person agrees.

lines.romaji: Un. Sore igai nara, nan demo.
lines.kana: うん。それいがいなら、なんでも。
lines.say: うん。それ以外なら、何でも。
lines.note: Sore igai: other than that. Nara: if it is.

lines.kana: きのうのえいが、どうだった？
lines.say: 昨日の映画、どうだった？
lines.note: Dō datta?: how was it? The past of dō?
Yokatta: it was good. Yokatta to omou is a strange answer: you usually know whether you liked a film.

tr.en: What did you like about it?

lines.note: Doko ga yokatta?: which part was good?
Etto: um, to buy time. Saigo: the end.

lines.romaji: Saigo? Emi, nete ta yo ne.
lines.kana: さいご？エミ、ねてたよね。

tr.en: The ending? Emi, you were asleep.

lines.note: Neru: to sleep. Nete ta: was sleeping.

lines.romaji: Ibiki ga kikoeta ki ga suru kedo.
lines.kana: いびきがきこえたきがするけど。
lines.say: いびきが聞こえた気がするけど。

tr.en: I have a feeling I heard snoring.

lines.note: … ki ga suru: I have a feeling that… Ibiki: snoring. Kedo leaves the sentence open.

lines.romaji: Me o tojite, kiite ta dake.
lines.kana: めをとじて、きいてただけ。
lines.say: 目を閉じて、聞いてただけ。

tr.en: I was just listening with my eyes closed.

lines.note: Me o tojiru: to close your eyes. Dake: only, just.

lines.kana: じゃ、はんにんはだれだった？
lines.note: Hannin: the culprit. It was a mystery film.
She sends the question back. Using the person's name instead of anata (you) is normal in Japanese.

notes: Asking: A, dō? (how is A?), dō omou? (what do you think?), dō datta? (how was it?), nani ga ii? (what would you like?).
Giving an opinion: … to omou. Oishii to omou, dezāto da to omou, yokatta to omou.
Softening: kana (I suppose, I wonder), … to omotte left unfinished, ii n ja nai? (looks fine, doesn't it?).
The polite no: A wa chotto… Nobody finishes the sentence. Dō kana is another one.
Liking one thing better: A no hō ga suki. Kinō no shatsu no hō ga suki.
A feeling, not a fact: … ki ga suru. Ibiki ga kikoeta ki ga suru.
Not choosing: nan demo ii (anything is fine). Sore igai nara: as long as it's something else.

questions.q: Riku wants Emi's opinion of his shirt. What does he ask?
questions.why: Dō omou?: what do you think? Nani ga ii? asks what you would like.

options: Riku put three apples in it.
questions.why: Ringo o ireta n da. Mittsu.

questions.q: Emi does not want ramen. What does she say?
questions.why: A wa chotto…: the polite no.

questions.q: What is funny about Emi's opinion of the shirt?
options: Riku wore the same shirt yesterday.
Emi has not seen the shirt.
questions.why: Kinō mo kore da yo: it is the same shirt.

questions.q: Why can't Emi say who the culprit was?
questions.why: Ibiki ga kikoeta ki ga suru: Riku heard her snoring.
